_about: Founder-declared parameter values. A value here is a POLICY, chosen for a stated reason; it is not a default, not a tuning knob, and not fitted to data. Code resolves values from this file and FAILS CLOSED when one is absent — an invented parameter is an ungoverned one. Declaring or changing a value is ESCALATE-ALWAYS (projectos.domain.tiers): a founder act, recorded here with its reason in the founder's own words.
_on_evidence: Some rows carry `evidence_consulted`. That is measurement which INFORMED the discussion, never the basis for the number. A value fitted to an observed distribution is a fitted parameter wearing a policy label, and this register exists to stop exactly that. Where a row has both, `basis` states which argument actually chose the value.

INBOX-AUTH-ENFORCEMENT.reason: Build the switch; leave it tolerant. Refusing everything unsigned before every issuer signs would refuse every legitimate assignment in the fleet.

semantics.tolerant: An UNSIGNED file may be acted on; the absence is still reported. A file whose stamp is PRESENT BUT WRONG is refused even here — a failed verification is evidence of tampering or a wrong key, and no transition excuses that.
semantics.enforcing: Anything that does not verify is refused and reported.
semantics.flipped_by: The founder only, by changing this row's value to 'enforcing' — a written act in this register. No seat flips it for itself and no code path writes this file.
semantics.when: After the key is distributed to every seat and Chat signs every assignment it issues. Must be 'enforcing' before the wake scheduler is armed (DC-7's closing condition).

FLEET-CLOCK-SKEW-TOLERANCE.reason: One minute is the resolution limit of the stamp itself, so two minutes gives it one minute of slack for a single delay. Beyond that it is clock error, not rounding.
FLEET-CLOCK-SKEW-TOLERANCE.basis: The resolution argument above, and only that. The value follows from what a minute-resolution stamp can express, not from how the observed files happened to be distributed.

evidence_consulted.note: Consulted, explicitly NOT the basis. The measurement's only load-bearing contribution was confirming that the 60s floor is real.
evidence_consulted.caveat: The large values in this sample are Drive-synced files whose local mtime is the sync write, not the authoring moment. This is why the check is split by anchor (see scope).

scope.applies_to: Locally-written files, where the local mtime IS the authoring moment (measured ~1s skew).

synced_files.reason: A synced file's local mtime is the sync write, not the authoring moment, so this seat cannot see the fact it would need to check. Chat reads Drive's own createdTime/modifiedTime through the connector and runs the stamp-versus-server-time comparison each sweep. Recorded as owned, NOT as unimplemented and NOT as absent: a check assigned to whoever can actually see the fact is not a gap; a check assigned to someone who cannot see it is.
